newsitem.title: USA: SLIGHT CHANCE OF HEAVIER U.S. MIDWEST RAINS - WSC.
newsitem.headline: SLIGHT CHANCE OF HEAVIER U.S. MIDWEST RAINS - WSC.

text.p: Weather forecasts still suggest only light weekend showers for the U.S. Midwest but Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said there was a slight chance for heavier rains Friday and Saturday.
"The official forecast would be for 0.25 to 0.75 inch with 40 to 50 percent coverage," Burgio said. That forecast was slightly drier than outlooks released on Wednesday, he said.
But some weather models suggested another storm system that was drenching Kansas and Texas on Thursday could bring more moisture to Illinois on Friday or Saturday, he said.

"We're watching a couple of systems," Burgio said. "The cold front we've been talking about for the weekend, that particular front looks a bit weaker today so that would mean less rain. We also have another system that is producing some thunderstorms in Kansas and Texas."
That second storm was expected to move east through the Delta and into the mid-Atlantic states early this weekend.
"The problem with that is (the second storm) brings the moisture north," Burgio said.

"There might be an opportunity for some showers making their way into Illinois tomorrow and Saturday," he added. "If that moisture and the cold front reach at the same time, you could have much more rain than we're currently forecasting."
But Burgio said that second storm would most likely stay south of St. Louis and Cincinnati, missing the driest pockets of the U.S. Corn Belt.
Long-range forecasts suggested a weak front would reach the Midwest on Tuesday with a stronger one expected by next weekend.
Also, the National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook for August 12-16 was for normal to above normal rainfall and normal to above normal temperatures in the Midwest.
